metadata.title: Claude, Doc Extract.
metadata.purpose: Take doc-extract apart in the Teardown register: it doesn't read the file for you — it turns it into plain text. Name the trade-off: they optimized for a single, clean, mechanical job at the expense of doing anything you'd call understanding.

beats.narration_text: Liam here, in for Bear. Reasonable guess: a document skill reads the file for you — summarizes it, tells you what's inside. That's not what this one does. Take doc-extract apart.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'A document skill just summarizes the PDF.', hesitates on 'summarizes', corrects to 'extracts text from', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: A Claude skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. Open doc-extract and the whole method is sitting there in SKILL.md — plain language, no hidden logic, no secret sauce. Read the file, then act on the file. That's the shape of the thing.

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction set.

beats.narration_text: Here's the mechanism, in full. The instructions live in a Steps section — Claude reads each step top to bottom and runs it. No branching, unless a step itself says to branch. One document in, one plain-text result out. Nothing weighs anything.

Here's the actual job — the whole job. Turn a document into plain text. PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, RTF, or already-text formats: plain text, markdown, HTML. Not a summary, not an analysis — just the words, pulled out. They optimized for one clean, mechanical task, done the same way every time. Ask for anything past that, and you've stepped out of doc-extract into a different skill.

props.heading: Just the words, extracted.
props.body: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, RTF, TXT/MD/HTML
props.sparkLine: Not a summary. Just the text.

beats.narration_text: Turning a document into text, and understanding that text, are two different jobs. Doc-extract does the first one — cleanly, and only that one.

props.quote: Turning a document into text, and understanding that text, are two different jobs. Doc-extract does the first one — cleanly, and only that one.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: hand it a document — a PDF contract, a DOCX report, a spreadsheet — and ask it to pretend it's running doc-extract on the file. Before it does anything, walk you through the plan in numbered steps. Then run it, and show you the raw plain-text output. Watch where the plan stops. That's exactly where doc-extract stops too. Go deeper: hand yourself the same file, and now ask 'summarize what's in this document.' Point at the seam — the moment you stop extracting and start understanding.

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to understand what a Claude 'skill' actually does. A Claude 'skill' is a folder holding SKILL.md — a plain-language instruction set Claude reads and runs, step by step, before it acts. The skill I want to poke at is doc-extract: it takes a document (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, RTF, or plain text / markdown / HTML) and returns the raw plain text inside. Take a sample document of your choice. Pretend you're running doc-extract on it. Step 1: before doing anything, walk me through the plan as a numbered list of steps. Step 2: run it and show me the raw plain-text output. Step 3: point at exactly where your plan stops. That stopping point is what doc-extract's boundary looks like.
llm_exercise.dig_deeper: Go deeper: hand yourself the same document and now ask, 'summarize what's in this document.' Point at the seam — the moment you stop extracting text and start understanding it. Is that seam inside doc-extract, or is it a second job entirely?
